Based on the chest X-ray findings, which of the following best describes the characteristics and implications of the retrocardiac tubular opacity observed in this patient? Consider the clinical presentation of haemoptysis.

A) The retrocardiac tubular opacity is likely a bronchogenic cyst, which does not typically cause haemoptysis.
B) The retrocardiac tubular opacity represents a dilated esophagus, consistent with achalasia, unrelated to haemoptysis.
C) The retrocardiac tubular opacity is indicative of a hiatal hernia, which may cause chest discomfort but not haemoptysis.
D) The retrocardiac tubular opacity suggests an anomalous systemic arterial supply to the left lower lung lobe, correlating with haemoptysis.
E) The retrocardiac tubular opacity is likely an area of consolidation due to pneumonia, explaining haemoptysis.
F) The retrocardiac tubular opacity is a normal variant of the aortic arch, which is unrelated to haemoptysis.
